summary: The base implementation reproduced the timing-sensitive accounting defect in a deterministic regression: host_memory_budget_bytes used each rank's unsynchronized live reading while dividing by all co-located ranks. The correction synchronizes the reading with a MIN all-reduce over the multi-rank TP CPU group before applying the reserve and rank split; local, single-rank, and not-yet-initialized behavior remains unchanged.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression on the recorded base; the source lacked the TP synchronization helper and therefore could not perform the required collective. Raw output: reports/j-c4c21258a7da/raw/failing-before.txt
Seven focused tests passed after the change, covering the synchronized minimum and int64/MIN/group arguments plus local, single-rank, and initialization boundaries.
A real three-process gloo collective with divergent 74/50/62 GiB total available readings gave every rank the same 40 GiB post-reserve minimum divided by three (14316557653 bytes).
Repository formatting, lint, safety, and registered-test validation hooks passed.

gpu_execution.evidence: The issue is host RAM accounting and CPU-process-group synchronization. The assigned single gfx950 GPU cannot reproduce the reported TP8 H200 GLM-5.2 workload; no GPU or model-serving claim is made.

remaining_limitations: The reported 8xH200 GLM-5.2-W4AFP8 startup was not reproduced because only one gfx950 GPU was assigned and the model weights were unavailable.
Pipeline stages on the same host are not synchronized with each other because different stages may construct different host pools; the correction narrows the race to each TP group.
A TP group spanning hosts uses the group-wide minimum and is conservative, and ranks in separately launched data-parallel process groups remain outside ranks_per_host accounting.
